captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/24_beit, specifically its ViT-Base step 1 (models/beit_model.py, models/dvae_tokenizer.py, data/*, train_pretrain_beit.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Bao et al. (2021) BEiT, following microsoft/unilm/beit. The ViT is the lab's own (no timm); the MIM targets come from the frozen OpenAI DALL-E dVAE tokenizer, so this ports self-contained -- the only external artifact is a hash-pinned download of the DALL-E encoder.pkl (tokenizer_artifact below), and it is needed only for a real run. The port keeps the capture directory numbering (24) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (this list's number 25 is BEiT -- see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers

upstream.note: The dVAE tokenizer code only. Pinned as the submodule third_party/dall_e and imported lazily through PYTHONPATH (never copied or installed) to unpickle the DALL-E encoder.pkl for a real run. It has its own deps (requests, attr, ...) not in this port's lock; the hermetic smoke uses a random torch-only tokenizer and never imports it. The BEiT ViT itself is the lab's own code, not from here.

scope: The ViT-Base/16 step 1 is ported: a dVAE tokenizer turns each image into a grid of discrete visual tokens; a random block of image patches is replaced by a shared learned mask token in the ViT input; the ViT (LayerScale blocks) predicts the visual tokens at the masked positions, a cross-entropy over the dVAE vocabulary. AdamW under a cosine LR schedule with linear warmup; gradient-norm clipping. The capture's step 2 (ViT fine-tuning) is EXCLUDED, as in every port.
encoder: encoder.pt is the BEiT backbone trunk (patch_embed, cls_token, pos_embed, blocks, norm), producing the mean-pooled patch-token feature (embed_dim; 768 for ViT-Base). The shared mask token (mask_token) and the MIM prediction head (head.*) are training machinery and are excluded -- the standard SSL convention of probing the encoder.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the BEiT backbone's mean-pooled patch tokens (embed_dim, CLS excluded), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation). The capture's own BEiT eval fine-tunes the ViT end to end; this port follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than a fine-tune, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.

tokenizer_artifact.name: OpenAI DALL-E dVAE encoder (BEiT MIM targets)
tokenizer_artifact.note: Loaded lazily via the `dall_e` package (a pickled nn.Module) only for a real run; the hermetic smoke uses a random tokenizer and needs neither the package nor this download. Fetch and verify with bin/fetch-weights.py --artifact tokenizer_artifact.
tokenizer_artifact.sha256_source: measured on 2026-08-10 by a full download from cdn.openai.com; bin/fetch-weights.py re-verifies this value on download

rewritten_during_the_port: only the ViT-Base step 1 is ported; the capture's step 2 (ViT fine-tuning) is excluded, as in every port

the ViT backbone is the lab's own (LayerScale blocks, no timm); build_beit is a single construction path shared by the trainer, the tokenizer targets and the linear-eval loader, so the model is built one way
img_size and the ViT dims are threaded so a small hermetic CPU smoke runs a tiny ViT at a lower resolution

the dVAE tokenizer is the frozen OpenAI DALL-E encoder for a real run -- a hash-pinned download (tokenizer_artifact) unpickled by the `dall_e` code pinned as the third_party/dall_e submodule (imported lazily through PYTHONPATH, never copied or installed); the hermetic smoke uses a random torch-only tokenizer, so CI downloads nothing and imports no submodule
the blockwise mask generator, the mask-token replacement and the masked-position cross-entropy are kept faithfully (all torch)
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture called .cuda())
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch); the DataLoader gets a seeded generator

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, the AMP autocast and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32; the AdamW + cosine-with-warmup schedule and gradient-norm clipping are kept
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
